test_title: PYST 39: RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I - GA (Held On: 29 Aug, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: The Right to Constitutional Remedies, allowing individuals to move the Supreme Court directly for the enforcement of rights, is given under:
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 32**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 32** of the **Indian Constitution** provides the **Right to Constitutional Remedies**. This article empowers citizens to directly approach the Supreme Court for the enforcement of their fundamental rights.
 
• It is referred to as the **'heart and soul of the Constitution'**, as described by Dr. B.R. Ambedkar, because it ensures that the fundamental rights are not just theoretical but are enforceable in a court of law.
 
• The Supreme Court is empowered to issue **writs** under Article 32 to enforce fundamental rights. These writs include **Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Prohibition, Certiorari, and Quo Warranto.**
 
• The right to move the Supreme Court under Article 32 is itself a **fundamental right**. This ensures that citizens have direct access to the apex court for the protection of their rights.
 
• This provision ensures that the judiciary acts as a guardian of fundamental rights and provides a mechanism for their enforcement. *Hence, Article 32 is correct.*
 
• **Article 31**, as per the original Constitution, dealt with the Right to Property. However, this right was removed as a fundamental right through the **44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978**, and is now a legal right under Article 300A. *Hence, this is incorrect.*
 
• **Article 30** provides the right of minorities to establish and administer educational institutions of their choice. *Hence, this is not the correct answer.*
 
• **Article 33** deals with the power of Parliament to modify the application of fundamental rights to the armed forces or forces charged with maintaining public order. *Hence, this is not the correct answer.*
 
• ***Hence, the correct answer is Article 32.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Writs under Article 32:**

 
 
• **Habeas Corpus:** A writ that is issued to produce a person who has been detained unlawfully before the court and justify the detention.
 
• **Mandamus:** A writ issued to a public official or body to perform a duty they are legally obligated to perform but have failed to do so.
 
• **Prohibition:** A writ issued to lower courts or tribunals to stop them from exceeding their jurisdiction.
 
• **Certiorari:** A writ issued to transfer a case from a lower court to a higher court or to quash the order of a lower court due to a lack of jurisdiction or error of law.
 
• **Quo Warranto:** A writ issued to challenge the authority of a person holding a public office.
 
 
 
• **Significance of Article 32:**
 
 
• It acts as a safeguard for citizens, ensuring the protection of their fundamental rights.
 
• It empowers the judiciary to check the legislative and executive branches, maintaining the balance of power.
 
• It underlines the concept of judicial review in India, which is a cornerstone of the Indian democracy.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Article 226:**
 
 
• **Article 226** of the Constitution empowers the High Courts to issue writs for the enforcement of not only fundamental rights but also for any other purpose.
 
• While Article 32 is restricted to fundamental rights, Article 226 has a wider scope, as it can deal with cases of legal rights as well.
 
• However, Article 32 is a fundamental right itself, whereas Article 226 is a constitutional right.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• **Judicial Interpretation:**

 
 
• The Supreme Court has emphasized that the right to approach the court under Article 32 cannot be suspended except during an emergency as per Article 359.
 
• The court has also ruled that even if alternative remedies are available, a person can directly approach the Supreme Court under Article 32 for enforcement of fundamental rights.
 
 
 
• **Role of Dr. B.R. Ambedkar:**
 
 
• Dr. Ambedkar referred to Article 32 as the most important article in the Indian Constitution, asserting that it was the very heart and soul of the document.
